source_capture.interpretation: EDHREC inclusion is prevalence; High Lift is relative association, not a causal estimate of power or a mandatory inclusion. preliminary_judgments.reason: {R} 0/2 tap source: at three opponents one activation causes three total opposing life loss; this enables own-turn Abaddon cascade on hand spells printed MV0–3, but must survive summoning sickness and cannot replace same-turn Boltwave.

Cheap 0/4 repeatable all-opponent pings on cast instants/sorceries, including qualifying spells cast from exile; cascade-hit spells are actually cast but copied storm spells are not. Challenging huge double-cascade top-end may reduce ceiling.

Three-mana tapped rainbow rock with mana ability that simultaneously causes each opponent life loss: test exact cast/mana ability timing to determine whether activation paying for the very spell can raise Abaddon qualifying threshold. One-turn tempo slower than a two-mana Talisman, a real cost.

Cascade creature in graveyard returns to hand on casting spell that has cascade (including Abaddon granted), offering attrition, but five-mana repeat cast is clunky and cannot be assumed better than theme-identity random resource.

Discounted on creature deaths; refill eight and deal eight to each opponent is powerful, but 11 printed MV requires X>=11 to receive Abaddon cascade, and the eight damage only occurs after resolution, not retroactively for its own cast; discarding one's own hand and cost volatility are major risks.

Returns from graveyard to battlefield tapped on nonhand spell cast, of which Abaddon cascade produces many, but without sacrifices repeatedly it offers little compared with the 40K existing exile-spell token engine.

Four-mana creature plus three-mana tap activation adds a cascade grant to next noncreature spell; can stack with Abaddon but slower and narrower than already selected persistent Spark Double duplicate.

Existing M7 judged redundant wheel threshold against Bowmasters; revisit wheel independence/resilience rather than dismiss solely due to X above eight. Four-mana double-black setup has opportunity cost.

Two-mana upkeep symmetrical revealed mana values may cause opponent life loss before main phase, but only one target opponent, possible zero from lands, and user life loss from large printed spells; not proven better than pre-existing all-opponent sources.
High Lift 54x may reflect Warhammer identity and curated precon representation; do not invent mechanics or accept without exact source/slot comparison.
High Lift 53x alone cannot displace tuned cheap engines or payoffs; specific recursion and payable state to be verified.
Six-mana 40K creature with opponent-dependent coin flips is high variance and competes with deterministic life-loss/cascade payoffs. Verify actual source before final exclusion.
High Lift 52x could represent precon association rather than power. No claimed final disposition without verified current text and meaningful incumbent challenge.

They are not M7 final packages, insufficient under owner minimum-five-presentation policy, and cannot replace the locked 100 until whole-deck audit, stronger open-ended comparisons, actual mechanical/Oracle gates and explicit new exact-list owner decision.
